title: A notes API from scratch
idea: A custom JSON server needs a route table (an object keyed by method and path), a body reader and one `try/catch` for errors.

analogy.text: A help desk with one outgoing window. Every slip is read at the desk, and whatever the outcome, the answer leaves through that same window.
analogy.breaks: A desk serves one visitor at a time; a server overlaps many requests.

points: Each handler returns `[status, data]`, so every reply is sent from one place.
The body arrives in chunks: collect them, join them, then `JSON.parse` the text.
`JSON.parse` throws a `SyntaxError` on bad input; the `catch` turns it into `400`.
Any other error becomes `500`: log it, but keep details from the client.

steps.caption: The table has `POST /notes`, so that handler is chosen. An unknown route would get `notFound`.
`text` is a string, so the handler stores note 1 and returns `[201, note]`.
`send` writes the status and the JSON body.
The client prints the status and body. The note now lives in the server's memory.
A second POST sends truncated JSON: `{"text":`.
`JSON.parse` throws a `SyntaxError` inside `readJson`. Validation and storing never run.
The `catch` block maps `SyntaxError` to `400` and sends it. The server keeps running.
The client prints the 400 line. One bad request did not stop the server.

code.title: A notes server
code.caption: The whole server, plus a script that sends good and bad requests. Step through it, then press Run.

walk.text: `notes` lives outside any handler, so all requests share it. A restart clears it.
`send` is the only place a reply leaves: status, JSON header, JSON body.
`readJson` collects the chunks, joins them, turns the bytes into text and parses it.
Handlers return `[status, data]`. `notFound` is the fallback for unknown routes.
`POST /notes` reads the body, validates `text`, stores the note and returns `201`.
One handler per request: look up the route, await it, send. `catch` maps errors to 400 or 500.
The script sends five requests, good and bad, prints each reply, then closes the server.

pitfalls: Wrap async handlers in `try/catch`; an unhandled rejection crashes the process by default.
Cap the body size in real servers; `readJson` buffers whatever a client sends.
Check the type of every parsed field before use; never trust the body.

quiz.why: Valid JSON parses, so 201. Truncated JSON and an empty string both throw `SyntaxError`, so both give 400.

takeaway: Route by table, parse defensively, and answer every request exactly once.

starters: Why does the request body arrive in chunks?
What happens if an async handler throws and nothing catches it?
How would I add `DELETE /notes/:id` to this server?
